title: Ramp Probe Playbook — KPI Slate & Owner Log
summary: Living playbook for a staged ramp / traffic probe for new feature launches (models, routes, or infra changes). Combines a compact KPI slate, explicit owner log, short-term cost simulation, and a go/no-go checklist designed for fast operational decisions during a canary window.
context: Why: we need a repeatable small-run protocol that balances safety (quality & availability) and data for scale decisions (cost vs quality).
Scope: applies to hosted API feature launches and model serving rollouts where traffic will be shifted across variants for up to 48 hours. Not a product launch communication plan — ops-first.
Audience: product-ops, on-call SRE, service owners, solutions engineering for customer-facing beta toggles.
kpi_slate_rows: P95 latency (end-to-end) | <250ms | Redwood metrics / last 15m | infra-telemetry | >400ms for 10m -> page SRE
Error rate (5xx + model-timeouts) | <0.5% | infra logs / 5m rolling | serving-runtime | >2% -> rollback canary
Model regression rate (eval prompts) | <=3% relative drop vs baseline | eval harness hourly | applied-ml | >5% -> stop ramp
Token cost burn rate | <= $1.50 / 1k tokens (expected) | billing stream | finance-owner | +40% vs projection -> throttle/alert
Successful response ratio (app-level) | >=99.2% | synthetic probes | product-ops | drop below 98% -> investigate
User conversion lift (beta cohort) | experimental target | analytics | product-growth | statistically significant negative effect -> pause
Cache hit rate (prefix KV) | >= 35% | runtime telemetry | serving-runtime | <15% -> tune batching/caching
Autoscale headroom (GPU pool spare capacity) | >= 25% | cluster metrics | infra | <10% -> enable burst capacity
kpi_notes: Notes: focus on short-window signals (5m / 15m) for ops actions; 1h / 6h aggregates for product decisions.
Model regression measurement uses the canonical prompt-set (eval/prompts/ramp-probe.json) — include 'hallucination' and 'factuality' buckets.
Token cost burn simulated below assumes 75% of traffic uses full context (avg 320 tokens per call).
cost_simulation_snippet: Baseline assumptions: avg tokens per call = 320, requests per minute (start) = 40rpm -> hourly calls = 2400 -> tokens/hour = 768k.
Projected token cost: (768k tokens / 1k) * $1.25 = $960 / hour at start rate.
Ramp plan example: 40rpm -> 200rpm over 6 hours -> cost delta multiplier = 5x; estimate peak hourly = $4.8k. Keep buffer of 2x for unexpected payload growth.
Quick mitigation levers: reduce max tokens, enable prefix caching, switch to quantized variant while canary.
traffic_schedule: Phase 0 — smoke (10–15m): 1% of baseline traffic, synthetic probes + 2 small real-user cohorts; objective: validate routing & telemetry
Phase 1 — probe-hour (1h): 5% traffic, monitor 15m signals, confirm cost estimate; owners: product-ops and on-call SRE
Phase 2 — scaled probe (3–6h): increase to 20% if all 15m signals green; run model-regression suite every hour
Phase 3 — aggressive ramp (6–24h): move to 50% only if 6h aggregates stable and no regression trend; prepare immediate rollback window
Phase 4 — full rollout gating: require product signoff + dedicated infra commit for sustained traffic >50%

go_nogo_checklist: Pre-canary (must pass): telemetry pipelines good (no backfills), infra autoscale smoke OK, eval suite baseline uploaded, billing projection approved.
Canary window checks (continuous): 15m P95 latency stable, error rate below threshold, model regression within limit, cache hit rate acceptable, cost burn close to simulated.
Hard-stop conditions: sustained error rate >2% for 10m, model regression >5% on canonical prompts, unexpected cost > +100% vs sim for 30m, any customer-impacting data-exposure issue.
Post-window (decision): if all green -> schedule progressive roll to Dedicated window; if soft-fail -> pause and run 12h diagnostic; if hard-fail -> rollback to previous model & call postmortem.
runbook_quick_steps: How to rollback: run 'ops/routing/switchback --to=baseline' (see ops-playbook#switchback), verify synthetic probes recover within 3m.
Enable reduced-cost mode: toggle runtime-config 'quantized-mode' for the variant, reduce max_tokens to 128, enable prefix-only cache for large prompts.
Notify customers: template in linked_confluence 'Ramp Probe Customer Comms' and post to #pilot-support channel.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: sudden quality regression not captured by canonical prompts. Mitigation: add stratified random sample of recent real queries to hourly evals and increase human-in-the-loop sampling.
Risk: billing spike due to longer-than-expected responses. Mitigation: set cost guardrail alert at +40% and automated throttle policy that limits RPS if alarm triggers.
Risk: autoscale failure during peak. Mitigation: pre-warm nodes, reserve burst pool, and have SRE run contingency infra warmup 30m before planned ramp.
Risk: owning team unclear during off-hours. Mitigation: explicit owner handoff cadence in owner_log and a 1-click oncall escalation link in the runbook.
decision_points: D1 (after Phase 1): continue to Phase 2 if all 15m KPIs green; else investigate for up to 3h and re-run smoke.
D2 (after 6h at 20%): escalate to product for business-risk decision if any metric is marginal for 2 consecutive windows.
D3 (peak gating): require finance signoff if projected hourly cost > $3k for >2h.
open_questions: Should we add a dedicated synthetic probe for hallucination detection (yes/no) — cost vs signal tradeoff?
Do we want a hard throttle at token-cost-per-hour or a softer alarm that suggests throttling?
Which stakeholders must be tagged in the automated incident if model-regression >5%? Currently only applied-ml and product-ops are wired.
postmortem_triggers: Customer-impacting regression reported by >=3 customers within a 1h window
Unexpected cost increase >2x projection sustained for 30m
